## Summary

**PACKUSWB** (Pack Unsigned Saturated signed Word to Byte): Pack 2x4 signed words into 8 unsigned byte, saturate to 0..255.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `b & d convert → <vea>` |
| Syntax | `PACKUSWB b,d,<vea>` |
| Short | Pack 2x4 signed words into 8 unsigned byte, saturate to 0..255 |
| Description | Convert signed words to unsigned bytes. Result is saturated/limited when over the limit. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–0 | `00000110` |

- Not allowed &lt;vea&gt; : #imm

### Example

```asm
    packuswb    d0,d1,(a2)
```

```text
b d0: F8 00 07 E0 00 FE 00 12
d d1: 00 01 00 02 00 03 45 67
Result:
```

- vea (a2) memory content where a2 points to

```text
00 FF FE 12 01 02 03 FF
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no PACKUSWB. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use an immediate `<vea>`.
